aus_net_help:
Attention:
1. Emergency Backstop Application:
If the consumer applies to participate in the Emergency Backstop system, please tick "Emergency Backstop".
Ensure:
a. SPA (Solar Pre-Approval) is completed before submitting the NMI in Cloud/APP.
b. The NMI has not been previously registered with Ausnet and is accurate before submitting.
2. DER (Distributed Energy Resource) Registration:
Normally, after submitting the NMI in Cloud/APP, the DER (NMI) will be automatically registered with Ausnet.
No need for a third-party aggregator (e.g., Catch Power).
3. Testing on Agent Portal (Pre-Test Checks):
a. Before testing, set parameters to "in-band" (or automatic registration via manufacturer).
b. Ensure the Cloud/APP shows the NMI/DER registration status as "successful" before proceeding.
c. Test Conditions:
i. Wi-Fi dongle is configured & internet is connected.
ii. System software is up to date.
iii. Solar Export at least 1000W to the grid during testing.
iv. Some home loads should be active.
4. Test Execution & Results:
a. The test runs for 1 hour.
b. Click on "view status" for real time test status, result will be prestented when test ends,
5. Remote Testing (Battery Disabling):
a. To prevent test delays caused by battery operation, please contact AlphaESS support team to temporarily disable the battery.
b. After testing, notify AlphaESS support team to re-enable the battery.
6. AC-Coupled Systems (Battery Exemption):
a. DER registration is not required for battery storage systems.
b. Set the NMI through the solar inverter instead.
7. Hybrid-Coupled Systems (Solar Inverter Off During Test):
External solar inverter must be switched off during testing.
8. Non-Participation in Emergency Backstop:
If you have not applied to participate in the above project and ticked "Emergency Backstop", the system under this NMI will remain under Ausnet control.
9. Withdrawing from the Project:
a. To exit Emergency Backstop, contact Ausnet and provide the NMI for cancellation.
b. After deregistration, reapply for a fixed power limit as needed.

jemena_help:
Attention:
1. Emergency Backstop Application:
If the consumer applies to participate in the Emergency Backstop system, please tick "Emergency Backstop".
Ensure:
a. SPA (Solar Pre-Approval) is completed before submitting the NMI in Cloud/APP.
b. The NMI has not been previously registered with Jemena and is accurate before submitting.
2. DER (Distributed Energy Resource) Registration:
Jemena uses out-of-band DER registration. After submitting the NMI in Cloud/APP, please locate and copy the generated LFDI on this interface.
No need for a third-party aggregator (e.g., Catch Power).
3. Testing on Agent Portal (Pre-Test Checks):
a. Before testing, please submitt correct NMI and copied LFDI from Cloud/APP.
b. For the Jemena portal pre-test submission, the required information must include a screenshot of the inverter settings displaying:
i. Inverter Serial Number (SN)
ii. Safety Standard: AS4777.2:2020
iii. Regional Application Standard: Australia A
iv. max. Export Limit: 500W/phase
c. Test Conditions:
i. Wi-Fi dongle is configured & internet is connected.
ii. System software is up to date.
iii. Solar Export at least 500W to the grid during testing.
4. Test Execution & Results:
Test will be conducted remotely by Jemena, result will be sent after 5-10 days.
5. AC-Coupled Systems (Battery Exemption):
a. DER registration is not required for battery storage systems.
b. Set the NMI through the solar inverter instead.
6. Hybrid-Coupled Systems (Solar Inverter Off During Test):
External solar inverter must be switched off during testing.
7. Non-Participation in Emergency Backstop:
If you have not applied to participate in the above project and ticked "Emergency Backstop", the system under this NMI will remain under Jemena control.
8. Withdrawing from the Project:
a. To exit Emergency Backstop, contact Jemena and provide the NMI for cancellation.
b. After deregistration, reapply for a fixed power limit as needed.

register_dynamic_export_help:
Attention:
1. Please apply to participate in the SA Flexible Export system and check "Yes";
2. As the NMI is bound to serial number during registration, please make sure the NMI is accurate before submitting your confirmation;
3. If you have not applied to participate in the above project and ticked "Yes", your system under this NMI will be under the control of SAPN;
4. If you need to withdraw from the project, please contact SAPN and provide your NMI to assist you in canceling the registration of this NMI, in order to exit Flexible Export, and reapply for a fixed power limit.
sapn_help:
Attention:
1. Flexible Limit Application:
If the consumer applies to participate in the Emergency Backstop system, please tick "Flexible Limit".
Make sure the NMI has not been previously registered with SAPN and is accurate before submitting.
2. DER (Distributed Energy Resource) Registration:
Normally, after submitting the NMI in Cloud, the DER (NMI) will be automatically registered with SAPN.
No need for a third-party aggregator (e.g., Catch Power).
3. Testing on Agent Portal (Pre-Test Checks):
a. Ensure the Cloud shows the NMI/DER registration status as "successful" before proceeding.
b. Test Conditions:
i. Wi-Fi dongle is configured & internet is connected.
ii. System software is up to date.
iii. Solar Export at least 1000W to the grid during testing.
4. Test Execution & Results:
a. The test runs for 5-10 minutes.
b. Results (PASS/FAIL) will appear on SAPN's portal upon completion.
5. Loads & Battery Management During Testing:
a. To prevent test delays caused by loads or battery operation, turn off the loads and battery if necessary. Restart the battery after the test concludes.
b. For remote testing:
i. Contact AlphaESS support team to temporarily disable the battery before testing.
ii. Once testing is complete, notify AlphaESS support team to reactivate the battery.
6. Non-Participation in Flexible Limit:
If you have not applied to participate in the above project and ticked "Flexible Limit", the system under this NMI will remain under SAPN control.
7. Withdrawing from the Project:
a. To exit Flexible Limit, contact SAPN and provide the NMI for cancellation.
b. After deregistration, reapply for a fixed power limit as needed.
